one_line: A browser simulator for benchmarking routing policies across heterogeneous inference workers.
what_it_does: Configures simulated workers and workloads, runs Round Robin versus inference-aware routing, and exposes latency, throughput, queues, and utilization to humans and agents.
leverage_rationale: Domain-level tools can configure, benchmark, compare, inspect bottlenecks, and apply routing strategies against shared simulator state more reliably than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Frame sheet shows heterogeneous-worker configuration and an Agent Activity panel.
Frame sheet shows a run-simulation workflow and worker/result dashboard.
Description specifies shared state and domain actions for benchmarks and bottlenecks.
execution_rationale: The frames show a coherent, intentionally designed simulator with worker configuration, empty/run states, and activity tracking; result depth is somewhat limited by contact-sheet resolution.
execution_evidence: Visible worker/test cards and profile parameters.
Visible run-simulation prompt and Agent Activity states.
Description enumerates metrics and comparison workflow.
impact_rationale: Inference practitioners and infrastructure developers have a concrete need to understand routing on heterogeneous capacity; the simulator makes that tradeoff inspectable without hardware.
impact_evidence: Description identifies heterogeneous inference routing as the problem.
Visible dashboard is structured around workers, queues, utilization, and simulation results.
creativity_rationale: A focused infrastructure lab turns WebMCP into an operational interface for routing experiments, with a meaningful shared-state agent workflow.
creativity_evidence: Combines browser simulation, routing-policy comparison, and agent-operated infrastructure controls.
usability_note: Clear dashboard structure and activity feedback; dense configuration may still require domain knowledge.
red_flags: Contact sheets do not clearly show an end-to-end completed benchmark result.
standouts: Strong domain-specific WebMCP surface rather than generic click automation.
Shared agent activity and simulation state.
advance_reason: Strong, clearly scoped infrastructure product with substantial WebMCP leverage and credible demonstrated UI.

what_it_does: Imports local datasets, explores tables, applies filters and metrics, and builds charts with UI and WebMCP actions sharing one workspace and undo history.
leverage_rationale: An agent operates on structured datasets, visualizations, filters, metrics, and annotations through the same action dispatcher as the human, avoiding brittle visual manipulation.

Description states UI and WebMCP share action dispatch and undo/redo state.

Multiple configuration states culminate in a bar chart.

impact_rationale: Analysts and teams benefit from a local, shared canvas where agent analysis remains visible and editable rather than trapped in chat.
impact_evidence: Frames show usable table-to-chart workflow.
Description identifies shared human-agent analytics as the core use case.
creativity_rationale: The shared action/history architecture is a thoughtful synthesis of local analytics and agent collaboration, though visual analytics itself is established.
creativity_evidence: One workspace and undo model for both UI and WebMCP actions.
usability_note: Import-to-chart flow is legible; dense configuration can be demanding.
red_flags: Contact sheets visibly prove product workflow but not an agent call itself.
standouts: Strong visible end-to-end data workflow.
Shared state and undo are especially relevant to agent collaboration.
advance_reason: Coherent product with strong execution and meaningful WebMCP/state-sharing value.

leverage_rationale: Structured tools make multi-step scanning, capability changes, and verification more reliable than driving a builder visually, but the core workflow remains possible through ordinary automation.

one_line: A shared, user-controlled memory layer that carries preferences across agent-native sites.
what_it_does: Stores, audits, edits, and deletes structured preferences written by one WebMCP site and consumed by another to configure work automatically.
leverage_rationale: Cross-site shared memory is the product; WebMCP provides the declared read/write capability and shared state that ordinary UI automation cannot reproduce comparably reliably.

execution_evidence: Frames show cohesive dark/orange product presentation and assistant workspace.

impact_rationale: People repeatedly re-enter preferences across tools; portable, inspectable memory addresses a broad agent-web friction while preserving user control.
impact_evidence: Description demonstrates six downstream configuration choices from one remembered preference set.
Control-plane edit and permanent-delete affordances are described.
creativity_rationale: A user-owned memory substrate for interoperable agent sites is a novel interaction and infrastructure proposition, developed through concrete producer/consumer demos.
creativity_evidence: Memory is shared across unrelated sites rather than sealed in an assistant.
The delete key and provenance model make governance part of the concept.
usability_note: The cross-site concept is compelling; memory management and permissions may need careful onboarding.
red_flags: Frames emphasize presentation and narrative; exact tool-call/result details are not fully legible.
standouts: Strongest WebMCP indispensability in the packet.
User-controlled deletion and provenance are unusually thoughtful.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP premise with concrete cross-site demonstration and strong impact.

one_line: An interactive explainer that uses seven playful rooms to show how agents change website business models.
what_it_does: Guides visitors through seven website archetypes, lets an agent use each room's real tools, and closes the tools while displaying call receipts.
leverage_rationale: The project uses live page-registered tools, shared human/agent actions, ephemeral authority, and receipts as the explanatory medium; the experience depends on WebMCP semantics rather than mere UI clicks.

impact_evidence: Description frames the project as an interactive explanation of seven business categories.

standouts: Exceptional concept-to-medium fit.
Honest treatment of which actions are real versus ghost.
advance_reason: Highly original, WebMCP-native explainer with strong ambition and a clear educational audience.

impact_evidence: Description identifies a concrete learning/debugging problem.
